key_findings.text: Further tests showed that the ﬂames surrounding the binary droplet array at inter-droplet spacings of L ≈ 8 and 12 mm (merged ﬂames existed for both spacings) both extinguished at droplet diameters smaller than the single droplet.

An entirely quasisteady gas phase with rapid chemistry maintains a constant ratio of ﬂame diameter to droplet diameter during combustion, but already in early microgravity droplet-combustion experiments this was observed not to occur Kumagai and Isoda (1956); Isoda and Kumagai (1958); Okajima and Kumagai (1974a).

earth_applications: Insights gained from these studies can lead to more efficient and cleaner combustion technologies which are crucial for reducing pollution and greenhouse gas emissions.

By improving fuel efficiency and developing better fuels, these experiments can contribute to: 1) More sustainable energy production. 2) Future combustor designs with minimal carbon footprint, maximum fuel efficiency and less pollutant emissions. 3) Allow quantitative evaluation of the performance of future fuels in combustors through the development of surrogates (mixtures of pure fuels that simulate the behavior of real fuels). 4) Validation of jet engine models by engine manufacturers with support from prior droplet results.
